name: Andorra
summary: Andorra is outside the EU and EU citizens have no free movement there: everyone needs a permit. The main route for people who do not work is passive residence, which since Law 2/2026 requires an investment of EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets (or EUR 800,000 in a home) plus a non-refundable EUR 50,000 payment, and 90 days a year in Andorra. Working and self-employed permits are quota-limited.
naturalisation: Reported 20 years of continuous residence for ordinary naturalisation (earlier research, not re-verified this session).
dual_citizenship_note: Andorran nationality generally requires renouncing the previous nationality (not re-verified this session).

routes.investment_options: EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets; or EUR 800,000 in one residential property; reported alternative of EUR 400,000 to the Housing Fund (not confirmed from the law text).
routes.fees_note: Non-refundable AFA payment, EUR 12,000 per dependent. An immigration fee of EUR 2,500 (EUR 500 per dependent) is reported by one source only.
routes.family: Spouse and dependents included for EUR 12,000 each.
routes.tax_note: Passive residents can become tax resident after 183 days; Andorra income tax is 0% to 10%. A permit alone does not make you tax resident.
routes.name: Passive residence (residència sense activitat lucrativa)
routes.summary: A residence permit without the right to work, for people who invest EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets or buy a home, pay a non-refundable EUR 50,000 and spend at least 90 days a year in Andorra.
routes.requirements: As reported for Law 2/2026 (in force 13 February 2026 per Andorra Insiders; approved by the Consell General on 22 January 2026): invest at least EUR 1,000,000 in Andorran assets (financial instruments, debt, funds, stakes in local companies; raised from EUR 600,000), or buy one residential property worth at least EUR 800,000 (raised from EUR 600,000), or, as reported, contribute EUR 400,000 to the state Housing Fund; non-refundable payment to the Andorran Financial Authority (AFA) of EUR 50,000 for the main applicant and EUR 12,000 per dependent (previously a refundable deposit); health insurance; clean record; no work in Andorra. Applications filed before the law took effect are processed under the old rules.
routes.physical_presence: At least 90 days a year in Andorra

routes.name: Active residence: employment or self-employment
routes.summary: Foreigners can live and work in Andorra with an employment or self-employment permit; the number of permits is limited by quota.
routes.requirements: Quota system applies to employed and self-employed permits; self-employed applicants must meet business and financial conditions (non-refundable payment exemptions exist for digital economy, entrepreneurship and innovation projects, per BDO). Thresholds not sourced.

routes.name: Digital nomad residence permit
routes.summary: A special residence permit for remote workers employed by a foreign company, reported to be available since 2023 under Law 42/2022.
routes.requirements: As reported by a consultancy, not an official page: sufficient financial means for the applicant and dependants, comprehensive health insurance, commitment to make Andorra the main and effective residence for 90 days a year or more. Initial permit 2 years, then 2, 3 and 10-year renewals. Income threshold not sourced.
